subject: Clarifications: EU-US export assurance and operational safeguards for MedicoQ
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medicoq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: MedicoQ Legal <legal@medicoq.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial questions on export assurance / EU-US DPF alignment

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for sending over the draft DPA annex. Our legal team did a first pass and asked that we get a few clarifications so they can complete their DPF evidence pack. Can you confirm the following items (we’ve grouped them by technical and contractual):

1) Data residency and routing
- Do you support routing customer workloads (token processing) exclusively via EU regions? If not, what region controls or routing policies exist?

2) Export safeguards (operational)
- For EU->US processing under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, what concrete safeguards are implemented for in-transit/exported user content? Is there an operational runbook we can reference?

3) Subprocessors / transfers
- Can you supply the current subprocessor list and confirm whether any US-based subprocessors will have direct access to plaintext customer data?

4) Key management and split-access
- How are keys managed for encryption at rest? Do customers have the option to bring their own key (BYOK) or HSM integration?

5) Logging & audit evidence
- We need an example log extract demonstrating how requests are traced (request id -> model variant -> region -> timestamp). Retention period required: 12 months.

We’ve attached our DPF template for you to populate where helpful. Can we get a consolidated response by EOD tomorrow (Thu 16 Aug)? Our counsel (Oliver Shaw) will review and may follow up with a quick call.

Appreciate it — Claire

--

Subject: Re: Initial questions on export assurance / EU-US DPF alignment

Claire — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ve attached a short operational runbook and our current DPA annex extract for the items you flagged. Marissa and Monica are looped in for the technical snippets and log extract.

1) Data routing
- Routing controls: Customers can pin requests to EU-only endpoints for both inference and KV cache. Default hosted API is region-aware and will route to the nearest region unless customer requests EU-only through the "region_lock" flag (API + console option).
- We maintain EU region endpoints (Frankfurt/Amsterdam) and will not cross-route EU-locked traffic to US or APAC unless the customer authorizes.

2) Export safeguards / operational runbook
- We operate an "Export Assurance" runbook (attached: operational_runbook_appendix3.docx) covering: approval gates for fallback routing, encryption-in-transit, prefix/KV caching controls (automatic redaction for sensitive prefixes), and mandatory canary/fallback policies.
- For DPF compliance we provide an evidence pack showing: process flow, responsible owners, and documented fallback behavior when EU capacity is constrained.

3) Subprocessors
- Subprocessor list: attached in the DPA annex PDF.
- Direct plaintext access: By design, no US-based subprocessors have default direct access to raw customer prompts for EU-locked customers. Access to decrypted content is restricted to a narrow set of operator roles and requires Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation logged and approved.

4) Key management
- BYOK: Yes — BYOK via customer KMS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted customers can opt for Redwood-managed keys or use a partner KMS with customer-managed key configuration (coming soon as GA; pilot available).
- HSM: We support HSM-backed key wrapping for at-rest encryption for Private deployments and for Dedicated with enterprise contract.

5) Logging & audit evidence
- We can produce an anonymized log extract with pseudonymized request IDs; sample format included in the runbook. Retention for security logs is 13 months by default; application request traces are retained 12 months for EU-locked accounts (configurable).

Next steps / deliverables I’m attaching: redwood_dpa_annex_v1.pdf, operational_runbook_appendix3.docx, and a filled tab in your MedicoQ_DPF_template_v2.xlsx with high-level confirmations. Monica, can you attach the sample log extract (pseudonymized) and a short blurb on JIT access controls?

Ben

Hi Claire — attaching the pseudonymized log extract as requested (see: MedicoQ_DPF_template_v2.xlsx tab 'logs-sample'). Key notes:

- Each request record includes: pseudonymized_request_id, timestamp_utc, endpoint_region, model_id, model_variant, processing_node_id. No user-PII is present in the sample output.
- JIT access: operators requesting access to decrypted request contents must submit a ticket (ticket id recorded), an owner approves (two-person approval for EU-locked accounts) and the read is time-limited to 15 minutes with a recorded session capture.
- Access to keys: operator roles do NOT hold key material; KMS calls are audited and returns are ephemeral handles that are not persisted.

Attachment note: the full subprocessor CSV is in the DPA annex PDF; the short list of US subprocessors that perform infra provisioning (no default data access) is summarized in the annex.

If helpful, we can redact and send an actual red-team-style capture proving the audit trail; otherwise the runbook + log extract should meet counsel's needs for now.

Regards,
Monica
